coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Mission Rock Block H
record.summary: A flex block at the south-east corner of the site on Mission Rock Street and Terry A. Francois Boulevard, developable as either commercial (90 ft) or residential (120 ft) with a special-feature corner. No source read reports construction on it. The Port's June 2026 Phase 2 report does not name this block; the Commission approved up to $10 million of Phase 2 pre-development funding on June 9, 2026 (minutes). It sits in the last of the EIR's four illustrative construction areas.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE (planned, unbuilt block): no Assessor lot of its own yet. It sits on lot 8719A006, the ~37,400 m2 undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 that also holds Blocks C, D, E, H, I, J, Mission Rock Square, Channel Lane and the unbuilt internal streets. Traced 2026-09-17 from the adopted Design Controls' Figure 6.2 through a transform with 0.7 m RMS residual on 16 real lot corners, with vertices snapped to recorded lot lines where the figure draws the block against one: treat street-facing and lot-line edges as accurate to ~1 m and interior edges (against unbuilt streets and open spaces) to ~1-3 m. The block's shape is the Design Controls' block, not a building footprint; a building may sit back from these lines.
notes.digitized_from: Mission Rock Design Controls (Port of San Francisco, dated April 24, 2018), Figure 6.2 - Maximum Height Plan (p.151); land use from Figure 1.1 - Land Use Plan (p.10); block corners snapped to the recorded DataSF Assessor lot lines of the 2020 Seawall Lot 337 subdivision where they fall within 3 m.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor lot exists under this block -- 8719A006, the undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 recorded 2020-06-12 -- but it has not been subdivided per block, so using that lot would paint the same ~9-acre parking-lot shape for every unbuilt block. Hand-derived geometry is used instead, with the lot's own lines wherever this block touches them.
notes.regulatory_context: Flex block (Residential Mixed Use or Commercial Mixed Use, developer's choice) per the Design Controls (Table 6.4, 'BLOCK H (FLEX)'). Max height 90 ft if built commercial, 120 ft if built residential -- the '*90'/120'' notation in Figure 6.2. Southernmost block on the Bridgeview St/Terry A. Francois Blvd side, fronting Mission Rock Street.

changes.text: The Port's June 2026 report on Phase 2 does not name Block H; the Port Commission approved up to $10 million of Phase 2 pre-development funding on June 9, 2026, and no source read reports construction on this block. The Board of Supervisors' own records date the Mission Rock DDA approval (Resolution 42-18) to February 13, 2018 and the final passage of the Development Agreement ordinance (No. 33-18) to February 27, 2018; the Notice of Determination gives March 6, 2018 as the City's approval date and lists the Board's EIR action (File 171286) among its final actions. The Port's fact sheet lists August 15, 2018 as the Development Agreement's effective date, and the Planning page dates the DDA 8/15/2018. The Port's January 2018 staff report describes the DDA's outside dates for starting later phases (a legal deadline, not a forecast); the DDA text itself has not been read, so no calendar date is given. The Port's June 2026 report schedules the Developer's Phase 2 Submittal for Winter/Spring 2027 and a possible construction start for Summer/Fall 2027 (expected dates); no source read reports construction or a vertical design submittal for this block or states its current use. DDA-specific section numbers and target dates previously listed here are removed because the DDA text has not been read.

open_questions: Whether Block H will be built residential or commercial has not been decided in any document read.

The Port's June 5, 2026 report schedules the Developer's Phase 2 Submittal ('proposal for Phase 2 including development summary and Phase budget') for Winter/Spring 2027 and a 'Potential Construction Start' for Summer/Fall 2027 (Table 2; expected dates, not events). No source read reports a construction start, a Phase 2 budget approval or a vertical design submittal for this block, and none states the block's current use; the Developer's July 2019 Phase 1 overview forecast that Lot A, the remainder of Seawall Lot 337, would keep serving parking pending future-phase construction.
Which blocks the December 2022 Phase 2 Submittal covers is not stated in the Port memos read; only the Phase 2 parking garage is named.

The Port's January 26, 2018 staff report (Table 3, DDA Major Terms) describes the DDA's outside date for commencing construction of each later Phase as 'the earlier of 5 years after completion of vertical construction of the prior Phase or 14 years after the Entitlement Date for Phase 2, 20 years after the Entitlement Date for Phase 3, and 25 years after the Entitlement Date for Phase 4'. These are legal deadlines, not forecasts. The DDA text itself was not read, so no calendar date is derived here.
No cost, developer capital or land-value figure exists for this block; the Port says Phase 2 appraisals are deferred until the market supports the minimum land values.

Images: no rendering specific to this block exists in the public-record documents read (the Design Controls give only diagrammatic envelopes), and the 2026 aerial serves as the 'before'/'now' view of the parking lot it sits in.

No expected-completion date could be sourced for Block H. The Mission Rock Design Controls (208 pages, checked in full) contain no phasing schedule at all. The Draft EIR's illustrative phasing (April 2017) placed Block H in Area 4 (2020-2023), a different scheme from the DDA's four Phases, and no document read states which DDA Phase includes Block H. The DDA text itself (Board File 180092, adopted by the Board of Supervisors as Resolution 42-18 on February 13, 2018) was not read, so its Land Use Table and Schedule of Performance target dates are not cited here. Phase 2 was found 'not currently financially feasible' in October 2023, per this record's own milestones. No later Port memo, Design Controls revision or news source gives a revised target year for the Project's full buildout, so no basis (record, phase or project) supports an expected-completion date for this block.
